note: Sunday 07:00 SGT weekend run (day 2 of the weekend), after the Fri 31 Jul US close (markets shut Sat/Sun). July ended on a two-day RELIEF RALLY: Fri 31 Jul the S&P 500 rose +0.70% to a record 7,489.72, the Nasdaq +1.00% to 25,373.85 and the Dow +0.53% to 52,485.03 — all three posted weekly gains and the Dow logged a fourth straight winning month, capping a volatile July. Amazon jumped ~15% on the AWS +37% blowout and the four megacap hyperscalers now guide to a combined $720-745bn of 2026 capex, re-validating the AI-spend thesis that the prior week's >$1trn semis rout had doubted; Apple fell ~7% on soft Services/China. The catch: bonds kept selling off — the 10Y hit ~4.73%, its highest in over a year, on sticky June core PCE (+3.3% y/y) and a hawkish-hold Fed, and after the hot PCE September-hike odds ROSE to ~60-65% (CME FedWatch ~63%+, prediction markets ~53%), up from ~53-61% a week earlier. VIX collapsed to 15.99 (-6.4%, from a 17.09 prior close) as equity fear drained even as rate risk built. Weekend tape: Fri's hot PCE lifted the USD to a 3-week high and knocked the metals off their highs — gold slipped ~1.5% to ~$4,043-4,054 and silver ~2.2% to ~$57.8 into the weekend (both still near record/multi-year ground); oil firmed after a Qatari-LNG tanker (Gaslog Shanghai) was struck transiting the Strait of Hormuz on 1 Aug (Iran's IRGC also claimed it stopped two vessels and turned four back), WTI ~$84.67 / Brent ~$90.12 Fri close — the US-Iran pause stays broken though a 10-day ceasefire proposal is floated (Iran denies agreeing). Crypto softened over the weekend: BTC ~$63k, ETH ~$1,865, crypto Fear&Greed 27 ('Fear', from 33). CNN equity Fear&Greed last printed ~39 ('Fear') on 31 Jul; the dashboard fetches it LIVE in-browser (this baked value is the fallback). Flows are LAGGED: the freshest verifiable BofA/EPFR Flow Show remains the week to 22 Jul — the week-to-29-Jul print was still not retrievable this run — labeled as such and pre-dating the 28-31 Jul round-trip. CNN exposes no numeric per-gauge value this run, so the 7 sub-components are INFERRED from the composite, VIX and cited internals and labeled as such.

[Inferred — mcoscillator/Barchart JS-gated this run]

components.name: Market Volatility
components.reading: VIX vs its 50-day moving average. The VIX collapsed to 15.99 on Fri 31 Jul (-6.4%), well below its 50-DMA and far from Wednesday's ~20.66 FOMC spike — a decisive de-escalation into calm. [VIX confirmed via Yahoo]

components.name: Safe-Haven Demand
components.reading: 20-day stock vs Treasury bond return spread. Stocks rallied to records while Treasuries kept SELLING OFF (10Y up to ~4.73%, a one-year high, on sticky 3.3% core PCE) — bonds gave no bid and money stayed in gold (~$4,045 after a Friday USD-driven ~1.5% dip); the 20-day stock-vs-bond spread stays fearful on the bond side. [Inferred]

components.name: Junk Bond Demand
components.reading: Yield spread between junk bonds and investment-grade. HY OAS stayed historically tight (~275bp area, roughly 15th percentile) with no material widening — credit shows no funding stress, the least-fearful gauge. [FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2, ~275bp]

breadth.note: Breadth firmed further into month-end: the two-day relief rally (Thu +1.7%, Fri +0.7% to a record) reversed most of the 28-29 Jul FOMC-selloff damage — longer-term participation stays a clear majority above trend (~high 60s% of S&P members over their 200-DMA) and the shorter 50-DMA gauge climbed back above 50%. The VIX collapse to ~16 and two straight advancer-led sessions signal broadening, recovering participation rather than a narrow melt-up. The tension: internals are risk-on while the 10Y at a one-year-high 4.73% and ~53-61% September-hike odds are a rate-side cap. Several sub-metrics (exact 200-/50-DMA close, daily A/D, McClellan level, net new highs) were JS-gated or lagged this run and are labeled approximate. The open question is whether next week's SGX/HK earnings and the delayed Flow Show confirm the risk-on turn or the sticky-inflation/hawkish-Fed backdrop re-caps it.

flows.narrative: The freshest verifiable weekly read (to 22 Jul, pre-turmoil) showed a decisive cross-border rotation OUT of developed markets and cash INTO emerging markets — above all China, which posted its record 3rd-largest weekly inflow ever (+$21.3bn) and drove EM's 2nd-largest weekly haul on record (+$29.6bn) on H2-stimulus optimism, while US equities bled -$7.2bn and Europe -$1.6bn. Cash left money-markets (-$33.9bn) to fund equities (+$30.4bn overall), bonds (+$14.9bn), gold (+$2.0bn, largest since April) and crypto (+$0.9bn) — a barbell chasing EM/China upside while hedging FOMC-hike and geopolitical risk. This snapshot pre-dates the hawkish hold, the Iran-pause breakdown AND the Thu-Fri AWS/MSFT-led rebound, so the next Flow Show (to 29 Jul) is the tell on whether the risk-on EM tilt survived the round-trip. BofA's Bull & Bear Indicator sits at an extreme 9.6 and the July FMS shows cash at just 3.6% of AUM (below the 4% contrarian Cash-Rule SELL trigger, active since May) — stretched-bullish positioning that both amplified the Wednesday drop and fueled the two-day snapback; the next FMS lands mid-August.

Europe joined the US on the outflow side as money chased EM/China — a pause in the 2026 pro-international tilt within the DM complex, with the UK outflow the largest since November.

Broad bond-fund inflows continued as investors added duration alongside gold — a hedge that pre-dates the post-FOMC yield jump (10Y now 4.73%, a one-year high); HY OAS ~275bp signals no credit stress yet. IG/HY split not separately itemized this run.
